name: Keiko Fujimori
role: President of Peru (since 28 July 2026); leader of Fuerza Popular; congresswoman 2006-2011
summary: Peruvian conservative politician and leader of Fujimorismo who campaigned in four presidential runoffs, winning in 2026. Her platforms combine a hardline security and order agenda, a market-based economy under the 1993 constitution with expanded social transfers, and socially conservative positions on family, abortion and marriage. She has distanced herself from some of her father's record at times (2016) while defending the fight against terrorism.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Plan proposes a single affiliation system widening public insurance (SIS) coverage, free care for cancer, universal telemedicine and access to services for all, alongside private providers.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: In the 2021 runoff debate she said her government would raise the minimum wage, without giving a size.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Plan decalogue: 'free market yes' with solidarity economy and protections; she defended the 1993 market model in 2011 and stresses private investment (80% of growth) in 2026. Also gives the state a guiding role.

public-ownership.rationale: Plan limits state oil company Petroperu to refining and distribution, sells non-strategic assets, and brings PPPs into regional electricity distribution; she attacks Petroperu waste in the 2026 debate.

property-fundamental.rationale: Plan decalogue lists property among the pillars of legal security she defends, and promises one million property titles; stresses predictability for investors.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Plan proposes a 'deregulatory shock', removal of 500+ procedures and positive administrative silence; this is aimed at bureaucracy and business regulation generally.

cut-welfare.rationale: Plan doubles Pension 65, Contigo and Juntos transfers, raises the ONP minimum pension and restores Prona; in interviews she says working social programs must be expanded.

surveillance-ok.rationale: She seeks geolocation and intelligence powers against gangs she would designate terrorist.

strong-leader.rationale: Rejected closing Congress ('not an option in any way') and says politicians must dialogue and build consensus, while wanting a government with strong leadership.

empower-police-military.rationale: Core of her platform: military and police patrols, armed forces on borders and in prisons, 1,000 new patrol cars, modernised police; says police and soldiers are persecuted.

rehabilitation.rationale: Plan has prison work, reinsertion savings and productive prisons, but also mega-prisons and prisoners working for food; proposals point both ways.

traditional-family.rationale: UN speech: believes in the family as an irreplaceable pillar of society and says imposed agendas weakened it; plan decalogue calls the family the fundamental cell of society.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Opposes same-sex marriage (marriage between a man and a woman) and in 2016 rejected civil union; in 2021 she backed only a patrimonial union. Plan rejects discrimination on sexual orientation.

abortion-legal.rationale: Plan decalogue: protects the right to life from conception; she has said she accepts abortion only to save the mother's life and told women raped to carry the pregnancy (reported 2016, 2021).

gender-social-construct.rationale: Said her government would eliminate the 'so-called gender ideology' from schools while stressing gender equality and equal rights for boys and girls.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: UN speech: 'we believe in respect for our traditions' and each people's right to its own history and culture.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Proposed immediate expulsion of irregular migrants who commit crimes and military control of borders against illegal entry; did not call for lower legal immigration.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: UN speech asks the organisation to respect the limits of a community of sovereign nations and not substitute national institutions.

free-trade.rationale: Defended Peru's free trade treaties in the 2011 debate (asked why Humala wanted to revise them); plan builds on the existing 22 treaties and export promotion.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

state-directs-investment.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

results-over-ideology.rationale: She judges appointees by competence despite prior opposition affiliations.

positive-liberty.rationale: She says government must supply basic conditions for personal advancement.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Plan commits to a fiscal deficit of 1% of GDP by 2031 and fiscal discipline, though it also promises spending increases.

class-collaboration.rationale: She combines better wages with sustainable firms and employer cooperation.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Section 3.2 promotes cultural industries together with heritage protection.

ban-interest.rationale: She defends removing lending-rate caps rather than prohibiting interest.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Plan promotes exploration and exploitation of hydrocarbons with new lots in the jungle and northern coast, a northern energy pole and the southern gas pipeline.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: She describes institutions captured for corrupt private advantage.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: In the 2021 debate she said she rejects any possibility of forced sterilization.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: In her UN speech she said those who fought terrorism are still being judged despite due process violations and that human rights defence must not turn victims into defendants and perpetrators into protected persons.

night-watchman-state.rationale: UN speech says the state removes unjust barriers and provides basic conditions; plan and interviews expand state programs, schools, hospitals, pensions.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Plan decalogue and UN speech affirm equality before the law, human dignity and rejection of all discrimination, including by origin, religion and sexual orientation.

separated-powers.rationale: UN speech and 2011 pledge: true democracy rests on the autonomy and independence of powers; plan lists the independence of powers as a basis of legal security.

priority-to-poor.rationale: She prioritizes people excluded from economic progress.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: She describes multicultural Peru as one strong national community.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: She uses emergency regimes for military prison security and wider internal-control operations.

party-controls-media.rationale: She explicitly defends press and expression freedoms.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: She advocates deeper integration through the Andean Community.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: She expands US military and intelligence partnerships against organized crime.

death-penalty.rationale: Has proposed the death penalty for people who rape children under seven (reported from earlier campaigns); in March 2026 she said terrorism was defeated in the 1990s without it, so not for terrorism.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Supports teaching gender equality and equal rights, but wants education content on gender reviewed by parents and eliminates 'gender ideology'; mixed.

minority-language-support.rationale: Section 3.3 requires healthcare guidance adapted to local languages.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Pledged in 2011 not to convene a constituent assembly; in 2026 said she would be watchful if the interim president tried to, and defends the existing Constitution.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Pledged in 2011 and again in the 2026 debate and plan to defend the autonomy and independence of the central bank; warned she would act if the president threatened it.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: She says she would defend herself through judicial proceedings even as president.

patriotic-education.rationale: Plan strengthens civic curriculum with respect for family, national identity and civic-patriotic values; UN speech wants children proud of their country.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: She submits the budget and supplementary spending for congressional authorization.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Plan strengthens the national transparency and access to information authority and promises full public transparency of procurement.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Said in March 2026 that if she must leave the Inter-American Court to fight crime she will; UN speech stresses limits of international bodies toward sovereign nations.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Health plan promotes tariff agreements between public and private institutions so users can choose where to be treated, alongside public insurance; PPPs in infrastructure.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Her market platform credits the 1990s investment model with economic recovery and prosperity.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: The adopted Decalogue explicitly endorses popular capitalism.

assisted-dying.rationale: On the Ana Estrada euthanasia case she said life is defended from conception to natural death and that she does not share the decision but respects it, worried it could be generalised.

social-market-economy.rationale: Her party's program and her 2011 debate position both name the social market economy as the model, with rules for competition and protection for workers, small firms and consumers.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: She connects present Peru’s identity to ancient civilizations and Inca integration.

second-chamber.rationale: Says Fuerza Popular made a historic change in moving from a single chamber to bicameralism, to give political stability.

farm-price-support.rationale: Wants Prona revived so that the state buys directly from farmers when prices fall, and provides credit and irrigation to farmers.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Decalogue 6 requires democracy to deliver substantive public services.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: She emphasizes identifying poor households for timely assistance.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Decalogue 5 makes political parties foundational to democracy.

no-business-privileges.rationale: She condemns privileged procurement that undermines competition.

notes:
Positions are those of Keiko Fujimori herself; her father's record is not attributed to her. Same-sex union and abortion positions shifted between 2011 (patrimonial union) and 2016 (rejected civil union); the most recent clear statements are used. Debate captions have no speaker labels; only passages clearly hers were used. Reference sources on marriage, abortion, euthanasia and the death penalty are press reports of her statements.

Merged with an independent gpt-6.1-sol audit: 26 answers taken from it, 24 agreed, 0 conflicts settled by the integrator.

gpt-6.1-sol notes: Independent pass; no previous answers consulted and no living-person inference. Three of ten priorities answered: capitalist endorsement, historical market development, and legal interest. Full active list and nulls reviewed. Revolution, small armed-group theory, proletarian dictatorship, globally reorganized cooperative communities, and kin-peoples political union remain undocumented. Her condemnation of promoting class confrontation is not a historical-materialist theory; Marx’s quoted letter is not her view. Protecting life, private religious devotion and invoking God do not establish divine political authority. The inaugural address is a plan, not proof of achieved wages or pensions. The signed Lot 192 transfer is consensual contracting, not proof of overriding property rights; ownership remains mixed. Environmental monitoring and climate adaptation coexist with expanded extraction, so no nuclear, intrinsic-nature-rights or undamaged-Earth conclusion is inferred. Water restoration is not natural-capital valuation. The environmental delegation report was read, but committee opinions are not her words. AI flags procurement anomalies for human officials; that does not establish algorithmic government or extinction priority. US security cooperation does not settle permanent foreign bases or collective defense against every armed attack, and maintaining Chinese trade is not choosing China over the US. Regional integration does not establish ethnic or linguistic political unification. Military emergency functions are her own policy; her father’s coups and killings are not automatically attributed. Her antiterrorism prosecution objection is distinguished from automatic immunity for every police crime. The earlier El Comercio interview was read in full; its acknowledgement of autocracy and defenses of her father’s convictions are recorded context, not independent proof of his innocence. CIDOB records her 2021 annulment campaign and eventual recognition; no unconditional democracy-best answer inferred. Caption speaker context was checked against native-language reporting. No quiz-site positions used.
